implementation_sources.notes: Used only to cross-check the MTP input-fusion convention; it is not canonical Qwen3.8 checkpoint semantics.

supporting_sources.notes: Official but unversioned release article; not used to override pinned artifacts.

claims.claim: The checkpoint spells every fourth layer full_attention, while the released model semantics use QSA at those positions.
claims.source: Qwen checkpoint, technical report and Transformers
claims.notes: Transformers explicitly maps full_attention to qwen_sparse_attention; the report says all backbone full-attention layers were replaced with QSA.

claims.claim: The released architecture is Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration with separate visual and language modules and an LM head.
With both pixel-value arguments absent, the wrapper does not invoke the vision model and passes token embeddings directly to the language model.
claims.notes: Vision branches are guarded independently by pixel_values is not None and pixel_values_videos is not None.

claims.claim: Visual features replace matching image/video placeholder embeddings after an explicit feature-count check and use multimodal rotary positions.
claims.notes: Outside initial Kestrel-Q scope.

claims.claim: A language-model-only implementation can produce ordinary text logits without loading visual or MTP tensors.
claims.notes: Kestrel-Q must reject unsupported visual inputs/tokens explicitly.

claims.claim: The text model has hidden size 2560, vocabulary 248320, 48 layers, BF16 checkpoint dtype, SiLU activation, RMSNorm epsilon 1e-6 and maximum positions 262144.
claims.notes: Input embeddings and LM head are untied.

claims.claim: Embeddings are replicated into four residual branches, processed by 48 attention/GDN plus MoE layers, collapsed by a final GR read and projected by the LM head.
claims.location: report figure 1 page 2 and section 2.2 pages 10-12; Qwen4ExpTextModel.forward; Qwen4ExpForCausalLM.forward

claims.claim: The exact 48-layer schedule repeats three GDN layers then one QSA layer twelve times, yielding 36 GDN and 12 QSA layers.
claims.location: text_config.layer_types; README Model Overview; report figure 1 page 2
claims.notes: One-based QSA layers are 4,8,...,48.

claims.claim: GDN uses 16 Q/K heads and 48 value heads with 128-dimensional Q/K and value heads.
claims.notes: Tier B repeats each Q/K head three times to align with 48 value heads.

claims.claim: GDN applies a data-dependent decay followed by beta-controlled delta-rule erase/write and reads the updated matrix with the query.
Q/K/V pass through a width-4 depthwise causal convolution and SiLU; Q/K are L2 normalized; beta and decay are separately projected; output uses gated RMSNorm and an output projection.
claims.notes: Released output_gate_type is sigmoid.

claims.claim: Each GDN layer keeps recurrent state [B,48,128,128] in FP32 and convolution state [B,10240,4] in activation dtype.
claims.location: text_config.mamba_ssm_dtype and linear_*; torch_chunk_gated_delta_rule; Qwen4ExpTextGatedDeltaNet; LinearAttentionLayer

claims.claim: Prefill causally scans a sequence and commits final recurrent/conv states; cached single-token decode updates both once in place.
claims.notes: Chunk size and fusion are implementation details.

claims.claim: QSA uses 24 query heads, 2 KV heads, head dimension 256, 64 rotary dimensions and a sigmoid output gate.
claims.location: text_config attention and rope fields; README Model Overview

claims.claim: The indexer has four 128-dimensional query heads and one shared key head, pools complete blocks of four, selects up to 512 blocks/2048 tokens and always includes the incomplete tail.
claims.source: Qwen technical report and checkpoint config
claims.notes: Scores sum ReLU-positive query/key similarities over indexer heads.

claims.claim: Only causally complete blocks are eligible for top-k; selected blocks expand to tokens and combine with the visible incomplete tail to mask core attention.
Each QSA layer persists K/V [B,2,T,256] and raw index keys [B,T,128]; pooled block keys, scores and masks are transient in the pinned implementation.
claims.notes: State grows with context length.

claims.claim: Indexer KL distillation and sparse-training losses are training-only and are not part of inference logits.
GR independently normalizes four branches, uses a rank-320 elementwise dynamic read gate and writes each block output through one data-dependent scalar per branch.
claims.source: Qwen technical report and checkpoint config
claims.location: report equations 30-34 page 11; text_config.hc_count and hc_lowrank

claims.claim: Separate GR modules surround attention/GDN and MoE in every layer, and a final read-only GR mixer collapses the branches before logits.
claims.location: report figure 1 page 2 and section 2.2; Qwen4ExpTextDecoderLayer; Qwen4ExpTextModel
claims.notes: There is no H_res branch-mixing operator.

claims.claim: GR branches are current-forward activations carried across layers, not context-growing autoregressive cache state.
The report supports FP8 residual-branch storage as an optimization, while the released/reference default remains BF16.
claims.source: Qwen technical report and checkpoint config
claims.notes: FP8 requires future parity validation and is not assumed by Task 1.1.

claims.claim: Every layer routes each token over 512 experts, selects top 10, normalizes selected weights and runs width-640 SwiGLU routed experts.
claims.notes: Router softmax is evaluated in FP32 by Tier B.

claims.claim: A width-640 shared SwiGLU expert is sigmoid-gated and added to the weighted routed-expert sum.
claims.notes: Ten routed plus one shared expert are active per token.

claims.claim: Load-balancing loss is optional training/diagnostic behavior; ordinary inference needs routing IDs and weights but no auxiliary loss.
One PLE is placed at one-indexed layer 2 and uses ngram_size 3, eight heads per order, base vocabulary 20,000,000, embedding width 2560 and 128 table parts.
claims.location: text_config PLE/ngram fields; model.language_model.layers.1.ple.* tensor names; README Model Overview
claims.notes: The index contains 128 ngram_embedding shard weights plus PLE projections/state metadata.

claims.claim: Bigram/trigram addresses use current and preceding token IDs, EOS segment sentinels, deterministic odd multipliers, XOR mixing, per-head prime moduli and table offsets.
claims.notes: The checkpoint-indexed layer_multipliers tensor remains canonical and must be loaded/validated.

claims.claim: PLE projects lookup embeddings to branch keys and a shared value, gates the value from normalized branch/key similarity, adds a dilation-3 width-4 depthwise-convolution result, and injects it before layer-2 GR.
PLE persistently retains two token IDs and nine positions of dilated-convolution history.
claims.notes: Nine = (kernel 4 - 1) * dilation 3.

claims.claim: PLE lookup addresses are determined from token IDs before layer execution, and layer-2 placement is intended to overlap host prefetch with layer 1.
claims.notes: No cache/scheduler policy is selected.

claims.claim: The release contains one hybrid MTP layer, no dedicated MTP embeddings, and MTP attention configured at a full/QSA position.
claims.location: text_config.mtp; text_config.mtp_use_dedicated_embeddings; mtp.* tensor names; README Model Overview
claims.notes: The index contains 31 mtp.* tensors and the README reports about 4B MTP parameters.

claims.claim: MTP is used for multi-step speculative decoding and reuses QSA top-k indices across draft prediction steps.
claims.location: section 2.1.2 pages 7-9, especially table 4 and surrounding text
claims.notes: The report evaluates four-step speculative decoding accepted length.

claims.claim: MTP consumes a token embedding and a main-model hidden state through separately normalized/fused inputs before its one draft layer.
claims.source: Qwen checkpoint tensor inventory and sgl-project/sglang
claims.notes: Tier A does not fully specify exact fusion arithmetic or mtp_use_hidden_state_from_layer=null; verify before implementing MTP.

claims.claim: Ordinary autoregressive next-token logits are computed by the main text backbone and LM head without MTP.
claims.location: report speculative-decoding discussion pages 7-9; Qwen4ExpForCausalLM.forward and _keys_to_ignore_on_load_unexpected
claims.notes: MTP is optional speculative acceleration.

disagreements.summary: Released config uses full_attention labels; canonical report and Tier B implementation identify those positions as QSA.
disagreements.resolution: Preserve the literal label in source inventory but execute/describe QSA semantics only when all QSA configuration is present.

remaining_uncertainties.detail: Tier A and no-weight metadata establish topology and optional role but do not fully specify exact input-fusion arithmetic or the null hidden-layer selector. This does not block ordinary text logits and must be resolved before MTP implementation.

remaining_uncertainties.topic: optimized runtime precision and cache representation
remaining_uncertainties.detail: FP8 GR storage, derived QSA block caches and lower-precision GDN state require later parity evidence; Task 1.1 records semantics, not an optimization policy.
